I'd be careful reading too much into Space Force.

In the 1970's the Air Force Systems Command was responsible for all space operations. In 1982, it was merged with the Air Force Major Command to form "Space Command." In 1985 it was renamed the Air Force Space Command and typically referred to as US Space Command for short. It has over 38,000 personnel and hundreds of billions of dollars in funding.

A long standing problem has been the priority of funding within the Air Force between Air Combat Command, US Space Command, and other major command within the Air Force.

But separating the US Space Command and renaming it US Space Force, it eliminates the Air Force influence over spending priorities and gives Congress the authority to fund the Space Force separately.

And yes, US Space Command has many black development and operations such as the tracking and monitoring of all satellites and launches.

But I see this more of better defining the roles of the Air Force and the Space Force because most of the 38,000 personnel and the hundreds of billions of dollars in funding allocated to the US Space Command is simply a roll over to Space Force. But it is apparently more than a name change as Trump has suggested that Space Force will evolve from monitoring space operations to having control over offensive and defensive operations within space.

So, just as the Army is responsible for offense and defense on the ground, the Navy on the seas, and the Air Force in the air; Space Force will be responsible for offense and defense in space.

I was an Air Force brat when my father flew B-52's during the Cold War. Nearly half of the B-52 force was on airborne alert with nuclear weapons on-board in those days. I served 21 years in the Marine Corps and I spent over 20 years as a consultant supporting DoD high technology programs. I've seen the services morph many times to changing environments and threats.

There was a time with each of the services had control over their nuclear weapons. The Air Force Strategic Air Command, the Navy controlled their submarine launched missiles, and the Army in those days had tactical nuclear weapons such as the Davy Crockett, the Long Tom, Pershing Missiles, and the man packed nuclear devices that the Special Forces would use in Europe in case the USSR invaded, etc.

The Army eventually abandoned all its tactical nuclear weapons and those in the Air Force and Navy were merged into US Strategic Command which has control over all US strategic systems. The weapons still belong to the Air Force and Navy but US STRATCOM controls their use.

A lot of commands in the military have merged, morphed, disappeared, and newly emerged over the decades. The Space Force, in my opinion, is just a natural evolution of how offense and defense in the various environments are best addressed.

There may be alien technologies at Area 51, but my guess is that whoever is currently overseeing those highly classified projects will remain in control of them and Space Force will focus on the offense and defense within space.
